sources.citation: Breen, Gavan. 2009. The Biri dialects and their neighbours. Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 133(2): 219-256.
sources.note: The only modern linguistic treatment of the Mount Elliot (Morrill) vocabulary (Glottolog's classification source; AUSTLANG cites p. 245). Would confirm that nothing beyond the wordlist survives; a stress statement is unlikely but this is the one place a philological respelling with inferred stress could appear.

sources.citation: Gregory, Edmund. 1886. No. 125: Mount Elliott. From a pamphlet entitled 'Sketch of the residence of James Morrill among the Aborigines of Northern Queensland for seventeen years'. In E. M. Curr (ed.), The Australian Race, vol. II, pp. 448-453. Melbourne: John Ferres, Government Printer. (Glottolog ref 85832 = the bind1236 wordlist)
sources.note: Nothing. Curr summarises Morrill's ethnographic notes and re-keys the pamphlet's words into his Common Vocabulary (moongun opossum, koondoola emu, injin sun, wurboonburra moon, woggin/boolray/goodjoo/murrwool 1-4); plain English amateur spelling, no accent marks, no remarks on pronunciation.

sources.citation: Morrill, James. 1863. Sketch of a residence among the Aboriginals of Northern Queensland for seventeen years; being a narrative of my life, shipwreck, landing on the coast, residence among the Aboriginals, with an account of their manners and customs, and mode of living.. Brisbane: Courier General Printing Office. 24 pp. (JCU Library Special Collections, NQHeritage item 724; downloaded via the Internet Archive, scanned with tesseract at 300 dpi one page at a time)
sources.note: Nothing. The only remarks on the language (printed pp. 18, 20-21): 'each tribe speaking a different dialect.. I could speak eight of these dialects'; 'They have no written language whatever.. It is very gutteral in sound and extremely limited in power of expression'; 'The language is very irregular and seems to me totally impossible to systematise it in any way. The following is a list of the principle words'. The c.100-item wordlist (pp. 21-23: Nannie earth, Doongalla water, Ingin sun, Wurboonburra moon, Woggin 1, Boolray 2..) has no accent marks.
